CA-BERKELEY-EVICT-BerkeleyMuni.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code, Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance

CA-BERKELEY-EVICT-BerkeleyMuni.requirement_quote: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
tenant_conditions: The tenant owes rental debt, measured against one month of the HUD FMR for an equivalent-size unit in the applicable fiscal year.
CA-BERKELEY-EVICT-BerkeleyMuni.title: Minimum rent debt required for nonpayment eviction

CA-RENT-1947.12.title: Limit on rent increases

CA-SAN-DIEGO-ALG-98.1103.requirement_quote:
It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

CA-SAN-DIEGO-EVICT-98.0704.requirement_quote:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
tenant_conditions: The no-fault grounds include owner/family occupancy, withdrawal from the rental market, specified government or court orders, and demolition or substantial remodel, subject to the statute’s stated requirements and limits.
A tenant’s lease terms and conduct may determine whether an at-fault ground applies; these are not building facts.
CA-SAN-DIEGO-EVICT-98.0704.title: Just cause required for termination of tenancy

CA-SAN-FRANCISCO-ALG-37.10C.requirement_quote: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
